avatar.title: What your colours mean
avatar.text: Your bird's colours show the odds of what you would see if you measured it. At 70/30, measuring gives indigo about 7 times in 10 and violet about 3 times in 10. It is not a half-way color: a measurement always gives one definite answer.

gateDash.title: Gates are circuits
gateDash.text: Gates change a qubit's state. X swaps 0 and 1. H turns a definite 0 or 1 into an equal superposition, and back again. Z leaves 0 and 1 alone but swaps |+⟩ and |−⟩ by flipping the phase. A list of gates is a quantum circuit, the same kind you build in Qiskit.

ravensIntro.title: 1. Notes ride the wind
ravensIntro.text: The Sender Robin sends 32 notes. Each holds a secret bit, 0 or 1, and rides wind A or wind B. The Receiver Robin picks a wind for each note. When the winds match, the Receiver reads the right bit. When they don't, the reading is random, so that note is thrown away.

ravensIntro.title: 2. Peeking scrambles a note
ravensIntro.text: The Raven can intercept up to 16 notes and must guess each one's wind. With the right wind she reads the bit and the note flies on unharmed. With the wrong wind the note gets scrambled: the Receiver then reads a random bit. That is how a spy leaves a trace.

ravensIntro.title: 3. Storms flip notes too
ravensIntro.text: Each round has a storm that flips a few received bits at random. The Robins see a storm forecast, a range that contains the real storm strength. So an error might be weather, not a Raven.

ravensIntro.title: 4. Check a sample
ravensIntro.text: Both Robins' winds become public, and the notes with matching winds are kept. The Sender sacrifices 4 to 10 kept notes as a check: their bits are revealed to everyone. More checks catch more Ravens but leave a shorter secret key.

ravensIntro.title: 5. Trust or Abort?
ravensIntro.text: The Receiver decides. Trust: each Robin scores a point per key note the Raven didn't learn, and the Raven scores for the ones she did. Abort when a Raven was there: the Robins score 10 each. Abort when there was no Raven: a false alarm, and the Raven scores for her bluff. Roles rotate, so you play every part.

ravens.title: Weather or Raven?
ravens.text: Reading a quantum note with the wrong setting scrambles it. On average, a spy's peek causes an error in about one in four of the peeked notes the Robins keep, so spies leave a trace. Storms cause errors too, so the Robins must judge: weather or Raven? This is the idea behind the BB84 protocol of Bennett and Brassard. Error-correcting codes by Shor, Steane, and Gottesman fight the noise.
